headline: Maui County Liquor Adjudication Board

meeting.summary: The liquor board fined two restaurants: $1,000 with $750 suspended, and $2,000 on each of two counts.
meeting.recap: A restaurant pleaded no contest to one count, and the board found it guilty.[[0:04:05]] The department said the restaurant broke the rules by advertising five drinks with a six-course dinner for one fixed price.[[0:06:37]] The department recommended a $500 fine with $250 suspended for one year.[[0:27:00]] In a second case, another restaurant pleaded no contest to two counts, and a third count was dismissed.[[0:36:10]] An inspector found liquor stored in a next-door unit that was not on the liquor permit.[[0:37:44]] The restaurant's attorney said this came from disorder after the restaurant's emergency response to the August 8, 2023 wildfire.[[0:41:38]] The attorney asked the board to waive any fine.[[0:43:49]] The board met in executive session (a closed-door discussion) to deliberate.[[1:01:05]] Member Kim moved a $2,000 fine on each count.[[1:02:26]] The motion passed with five votes in favor.[[1:05:09]]
decided: The board voted to go into closed session to deliberate on the first case.
The board voted to recess and go into executive session to deliberate on the second case.
meeting.next: The first restaurant will be told when its payment is due. The second restaurant will be told when its payment is due. Members were asked to confirm whether they can attend the next meeting, which is expected to have a heavy calendar.

moments.q: Department explains the drink-pairing advertisement charge
Department recommends a penalty in the first case
Attorney describes the restaurant's wildfire response
